You shouldnt need higher octane than what the vehicle calls for. If you have knock from detonation when using the octane level called for by the vehicle manufacturer, something else is going on with your engine. You should find out what that is rather than cover it up. This could be timing, air fuel mixture, overheating, etc.

Octane requirement is typically calculated from two things. What is your compression ratio and if you have it how much boost. The higher the octane the harder it is to ignite the fuel.
Enough carbon deposits will absolutely change the ratio enough. I'm not saying you should cover it up, but most people with this problem couldn't afford a complete engine overhaul.

The only way I could see that being even remotely possible would be with a direct injected motor. That part that gets most fouled up in those are the valves. Even if we were to agree that buildup would cause enough of a compression change to require a change of fuel, there are plenty of remedies out there for combustion chamber cleaning that does not require an engine rebuild. Water being one of the most effective if used properly.

All that carbon coming loose at the same time could scar the metal, clog up the oil jackets maybe. If the engine is that far gone it might be worth getting another vehicle altogether. The octane boost is really just a stopgap measure.
